facts.label: Falar do tempo
facts.sub: Use It's + adjetivo para o tempo: sunny, cold, hot, windy. Use but para um contraste.

facts.label: Conversa sobre o clima
facts.sub: Falar do clima é um jeito leve de puxar conversa com vizinhos, motoristas ou pessoas na fila. Comentários como “Nice day, huh?” ou “Cold today, isn’t it?” pedem só uma resposta curta e amigável.

facts.label: Graus Fahrenheit
facts.sub: Os EUA usam Fahrenheit. A água congela a 32 °F (0 °C), e 70 °F é um dia agradável, em torno de 21 °C. Antes de viajar, converta os graus com um aplicativo para saber como se vestir.

pages.title: Four seasons, one city · 1/3
paragraphs: Hello from **Chicago**! I live here, and the weather is always a topic. People say, “**Nice day, huh?**” in the elevator, at the bus stop and in the café.
In **summer**, it is very hot and sunny. We go to the lake and eat ice cream. In **autumn**, it is cool and windy. The trees are red and yellow. Chicago has a nickname: the Windy City.

paragraphs: In **winter**, it is freezing! There is a lot of snow, and I say, “**Brr! Bundle up.**” I wear a warm coat, a hat and gloves. When it is pouring rain, I bring an umbrella. **It’s freezing out there!**

In **spring**, the days are warm again. Flowers come out, and the birds sing. Last week, I listened to “The Four Seasons” by Antonio Vivaldi. It is a famous piece of music from Italy, from about 1725. It has one part for each season. In the spring part, you can hear birds.

pages.title: Encontre a frase natural

items.why: English needs the subject It for weather.

opts: It is cold in Chicago in winter.
I am cold in Chicago in winter.
items.why: I am cold = my body feels cold. It is cold = the weather.
A lot ends the sentence by itself.

opts: In the summer is very hot.
It is very hot in summer.
items.why: Start with It is, and use in summer without the.
